To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal structure of a PKG Iβ cGMP‐binding protein domain (CNB‐B) bound to Rp‐ cGMPS reveals an apo‐ like, inactive conformation.

Rp‐cGMP, a phosphorothioated analog of cGMP (cyclic GMP), is an inhibitor of cGMP dependent protein kinase (PKG) and the crystal structure of PKG CNB‐B (cyclic nucleotide binding domain) bound to Rp‐GMP reveals an inactive, open conformation of the CNB‐B domain.

(1) Rp‐cGMSP binds to PKG Iβ in an apo‐like conformation; (2) the structure resembles the catalytic‐subunit‐bound inhibited conformation of PKA RI more closely than the cAMP‐bound conformation; and (3) Rp‐cGMP stabilizes the inactive conformation by interacting with a hydrophobic pocket in CNB‐B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and mechanism of cGMP signaling in PKG I.

the molecular mechanisms underlying PKG I activation and inhibition, which is of importance for the design of novel therapeutic strategies for diseases such as erectile dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, and cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of cyclic nucleotide‐dependent protein kinases (cNPKs), which are important regulators of many physiological processes, including cell growth, metabolism and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Rp‐cGMPs inhibits the PKG I β CNB‐B domain by stabilizing an inactive, apo‐like conformation.
Rp‐cGMPs inhibits PKG by stabilizing the apo‐like, open conformation of CNBs.
Rp‐cGMP is an allosteric inhibitor of cGMP binding to the CNB‐B domain of PKG Iβ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Rp‐cGMP and Rp‐cAMPs are not only inhibitors but also allosteric activators of cGMP and cAMP‐dependent kinases, respectively, and that the allosteric effect of Rp‐cGMPCs is more significant than that of Rp‐cAMPCs.
Rp‐cGMPs inhibits PKG by stabilizing the open conformation of PKG CNB‐B, which is a state that is similar to the inhibited state of PKAR1α bound to the catalytic subunits of PKA.
Rp‐cAMPs and Rp‐cGMPs are both potent inhibitors of PKA and PKG.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conformation of the CNB‐B domain is a key determinant of the activity of PKG I.
